resources.string:
Enable this plugin in Torque → Settings → Plugins.

Fix Fuel needs Android 5.0 or newer (Torque itself may still install on older Android).

After Torque binds this plugin, [FixFuel] Corrected Fuel Level appears under Settings → Manage extra PIDs. Delete any imported [FixFuel]/[OldFord] extra-PID rows whose equation is 0 (they stay at 0% and must not be used for Overrides). On the live Corrected row (value tracks the plugin, not 0) set Overrides PID → Fuel Level (From Engine ECU). Clear Ford’s override. Keep Use vehicle fuel level sensor. Do not override 012F with the Ford extra PID; Ford 16C1 is a source, not the override target. Dash gauges: Add Display plugin copy (non-zero), not the 0-equation extra PID.

Allow notifications when asked. On Android 12 or newer, also allow Unrestricted battery so Torque can start the plugin in the background. Then leave this app alone. Torque start / adapter / reboot will keep the plugin running.

Force stop (App info) puts the app in Android stopped state until you open it once — that is OS, not avoidable.
Battery/background start was denied. Open once so the plugin can run with Torque.

Add additional tanks as needed (stock tank 1 always stays). Do not switch senders onto the PCM FLI pin (false fill). Each extra tank needs its own Torque extra PID (MCU Mode 22, unique name — not 012F or Ford 16C1). Select-PID value is the 1-based tank id. Hardware: docs/fix-fuel-second-tank.md (CAN terminator off, short DLC stub, analog under dash; 1999 E-350 is J1850 PWM, not MCP2515 CAN). Gal/hr is charged only to the active tank.
